decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add, edit, open, and permanently delete bookmarks.” Round 1 client: “Saving a link, editing it… and being careful before permanently deleting… [is] the right idea.”
decisions.note: Conforming lifecycle decision at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “tags”; Round 1 client approves “tags.”
decisions.note: Tag assignment is included at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Search, filtering, and sorting.” Round 1 client: “search, filtering, sorting… [is] the right idea.”
decisions.note: The recorded basic search/filter/sort decision conforms; richer search is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker says only “duplicate detection”; Round 1 client approves “catching duplicates” without establishing whether duplicate saves lead to editing the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: At the initial specification gate, the presentation does not establish the reference-required convergence-to-edit behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly excludes “automatic metadata retrieval.” Round 1 client: “I expect the app to go grab the page’s title, a short description, the little site icon, and ideally a preview picture… that won’t work for me.”
decisions.note: The client replaces the exclusion with the reference-conforming automatic metadata behavior at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker’s proposed scope has no read-later state or view. Round 1 client requests marking bookmarks unread, viewing only unread bookmarks, and marking them read so they leave that list.
decisions.note: The client adds the omitted read-later workflow at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents permanent deletion without archiving. Round 1 client requests a reversible way to “tuck a bookmark away,” a separate set-aside view, restoration, and permanent delete as a distinct final option.
decisions.note: The client adds reversible archive behavior and distinguishes it from deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers only general search/filtering. Round 1 client says, “I’d also expect to search by a tag directly.”
decisions.note: The client requests the omitted tag-search capability; the transcript does not independently specify the exact UI syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers general search. Round 1 client requests “an exact phrase in quotes” and combinations such as “this tag but not that one, this or that.”
decisions.note: The client adds exact phrases and Boolean search at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes tags but no tag-entry suggestions. Round 1 client: “when I’m typing a tag… I’d like it to suggest tags I already use.”
Round 1 maker lists titles and descriptions but no personal note field. Round 1 client requests longer notes, readable rendering, and searching inside those notes.
decisions.note: The client adds rendered personal notes and note-inclusive search.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker does not present bulk operations. Round 1 client requests actions for “a lot selected — or everything matching what I’m currently looking at.”
decisions.note: The client adds both selected-item and current-filter-wide bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker mentions collections but no reusable dynamic search/filter view. Round 1 client requests saving a “search-plus-tags combination” as a named view.
decisions.note: The client adds the omitted saved-filter/bundle behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly excludes “import/export.” Round 1 client identifies the omission and accepts it: “import/export… I’m honestly fine leaving out for now.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly recognizes and accepts this departure at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker includes automatic title, description, site icon, and preview-image retrieval. Round 2 client confirms the automatic detail fetching matches expectations.
Round 2 maker includes “An unread/read-later queue” and read-state bulk changes. Round 2 client approves the queue and its defaults.
Round 2 maker includes reversible archiving, separate deletion, exclusion from normal lists/search, and restore. Round 2 client calls this the correct reversible “set aside.”
Round 2 maker presents search with tags, quoted phrases, AND/OR/NOT, and grouping. Round 2 client explicitly approves those search forms.
decisions.note: The presented advanced-search behavior conforms at the revised specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker includes “Existing-tag suggestions.” Round 2 client approves “tag suggestions while I type.”
Round 2 maker includes “Longer searchable notes with readable formatting.” Round 2 client approves longer searchable notes.
Round 2 maker includes bulk actions and states that all-matches actions include results beyond the current page. Round 2 client approves bulk actions with the affected count.
decisions.note: Reference-conforming selected-item and whole-filter bulk behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker includes named saved views based on live search/filter criteria. Round 2 client approves saved views.

Round 2 maker presents the revised first-release scope without page snapshots. Round 2 client explicitly identifies and accepts the difference: “down the road I might want the app to keep its own saved copy… I don’t need it now, so don’t add it.”
decisions.note: The client expressly accepts deferring local page snapshots at the revised specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker plans SSRF-resistant metadata retrieval. Round 3 client confirms the auto-fetching remains present.
decisions.note: Conforming metadata decision at the implementation-plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker plans a parser for phrases, tags, Boolean operators, and parentheses. Round 3 client says this lines up with the desired search.
Round 3 maker plans searchable, safely rendered Markdown notes. Round 3 client approves notes “showing up nicely and safely.”
Round 3 maker plans revision-bound bulk previews. Round 3 client approves counts that cannot change silently before confirmation.

Round 3 maker: “Full-page snapshots explicitly deferred; only bounded preview-image caching is planned.” Round 3 client explicitly accepts that the saved-copy idea is “set aside for later… exactly right.”
decisions.note: A later plan-stage presentation again makes and receives explicit acceptance of the snapshot departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker’s first checkpoint includes “automatic page details, graceful fallback, duplicate handling, persistence.” Round 4 client approves rich bookmark capture as the first increment.
Round 4 maker allocates tasks to “Search, filtering, and sorting” as part of the complete approved release. Round 4 client confirms all eight agreed parts remain included.
Round 4 maker allocates a task group to the “Read-later queue.” Round 4 client approves the complete task list.
Round 4 maker allocates tasks to “Tags, collections, and notes.” Round 4 client confirms the agreed areas have their own work.
Round 4 maker allocates tasks to “Archive and restore.” Round 4 client approves the complete task list.
Round 4 maker allocates eight tasks to bulk actions. Round 4 client confirms the complete release still contains all agreed parts.
Round 4 maker allocates six tasks to saved views. Round 4 client approves the complete task list.
Round 4 maker allocates tasks to “Individual editing and deletion.” Round 4 client approves implementation of the full release.
Round 5 maker claims rich bookmark capture is built. Round 5 client reports saving a URL and confirms a normalized duplicate is caught and points to the existing bookmark instead of creating another.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review decision, including explicit evidence of duplicate convergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker claims advanced search is built. Round 5 client reports testing search errors and says the advanced search coverage is present.
Round 5 maker claims read-later is built. Round 5 client reports marking an item read and confirms the read-later queue is present.
Round 5 maker claims tags/collections and notes are built. Round 5 client confirms “tags and notes” are present and cover the agreement.
Round 5 maker claims archive/restore is built. Round 5 client reports that setting a bookmark aside removes it from the main list, retains it in the set-aside area, and does not delete it.
Round 5 maker claims bulk actions with fixed confirmation counts are built. Round 5 client confirms those bulk actions are present.
Round 5 maker claims saved views are built. Round 5 client confirms saved views are present.
Round 5 maker claims editing and permanent deletion are built. Round 5 client accepts the application as covering the full agreement.

Round 5 maker: “Full offline page copies remain deliberately excluded, as agreed.” Round 5 client explicitly accepts the difference: the saved-copy idea is “for a future round… not part of this and doesn’t hold anything up.”
decisions.note: The implemented release deliberately omits local snapshots, and the client explicitly recognizes and accepts that departure at implementation review.
